# `proj ignore`

Choose which project paths Git or R package builds should exclude. Existing
user-written rules are preserved outside the managed block.

## `proj ignore add`

Manually appends one or more raw file or directory paths to the project ignore files.

Unlike automatic configurations driven by `_projr.yml`, these manual entries represent permanent, user-specified exclusions and are placed strictly *above* the managed `# Start of projr section` line.

### Arguments & Flags

- `<PATHS>...`: One or more raw file or directory paths to be ignored.
- `--force-create`: Boolean flag (default `true`). If true, creates ignore files if they don't exist. If false, skips file creation unless the project requires it (e.g. finding a `.git` folder or a `DESCRIPTION` file).
- `--type`: Optional filter selection (`all` [default], `git`, `rbuild`). Determines which ignore file receives the manual path entries. Note that `.Rbuildignore` is skipped entirely if no `DESCRIPTION` file exists at the project root.

## `proj ignore remove`

Manually forces paths to be tracked by appending negated syntax (e.g. `!path/` or `^!pattern$`).

These unignore entries represent permanent, user-specified negations and are placed strictly *below* the `# End of projr section` line in `.gitignore` and `.Rbuildignore` files.

### Arguments & Flags

- `<PATHS>...`: One or more raw file or directory paths to force tracking.
- `--type`: Optional filter selection (`all` [default], `git`, `rbuild`). Determines which ignore file receives the negated entries. Note that `.Rbuildignore` is skipped entirely if no `DESCRIPTION` file exists at the project root.

## When automatic rules are updated

Directory initialization and production builds update the managed ignore rules
from `_projr.yml`. Reading configuration (`proj yml read`) and looking up paths
leave ignore files unchanged. A preview does not refresh ignore rules, except
that a build or preview writing the starter `_projr.yml` also seeds the starter
lines and an empty managed block, as projr does.

The project is selected by `--project`, an inherited build context, or the nearest
parent folder with a projr configuration, else the current directory. See [project discovery](path.qmd#root-discovery).

## Git and R package exclusions

- `.gitignore` controls which untracked files Git normally ignores.
- `.Rbuildignore` excludes files when building an R source package. It is only
  updated when the project has a DESCRIPTION file; it does not prove CRAN compliance.

These files use different pattern languages: Git uses ignore patterns, while
R uses regular expressions. projcli converts configured paths for each file.
Check manual patterns carefully, especially when keeping a file that a parent
folder rule excludes.

## Your rules are preserved

Automatic rules are kept between the same comments projr uses, so projcli and
projr recognise the same block. Each tool's full refresh regenerates the whole
block from its own rules, as projr's `projr_ignore_auto()` does, so a projcli
build replaces rules projr placed there (and vice versa):

```text
# Start of projr section: do not edit by hand (update with projr_ignore_auto())
_tmp/**

# End of projr section
```

Inside the block, configured directory rules come first, then a blank line, then
other automatic rules (project metadata and planned render outputs). Any start
line beginning `# Start of projr section` followed by `:` and optional text is
recognised and kept as written; a comment such as `# Start of projr section
example` is an ordinary rule. Repeated, unpaired or reversed markers fail without
rewriting the file.

projcli replaces only the content inside the block. Existing rules outside it
are preserved. Manual add entries go before the block; manual remove entries go
after it.

### Starter defaults

When a `.gitignore` has no managed block yet, directory initialization, a
production build, or a build or preview that writes the starter configuration
first writes projr's editable defaults, then the empty block,
then the file's existing lines, so your later exceptions (such as `!.vdoc.keep`)
still win. Only defaults missing from the file are added:

```text
.vdoc.*
.DS_Store
Thumbs.db
.Rproj.user
.Rhistory
.RData
.Ruserdata
_projr-local.yml
_environment.local
```

A `.Rbuildignore` that is managed (DESCRIPTION or an existing `.Rbuildignore`)
receives the regular-expression equivalents `(^|/)\.vdoc\.`,
`(^|/)(\.DS_Store|Thumbs\.db)$`, `^.*\.Rproj$`, `^\.Rproj\.user$` and
`^_projr-local\.yml$`. These lines sit outside the block: edit or delete them
freely. Seeding happens only while no block exists, so deleted defaults are not
restored by later refreshes.
